scope: 30 exact historical keys outside other assignments; original operators and endpoint scopes inspected. Full pages 171–173, 215–216 and 331 re-read; whole draft 2FF subject inspected for inherited locator and phase accuracy.

rows.review_disposition: B888/0364/6773 must distinguish metropolitan constitutional royalism, pragmatic republican accommodation and divisions among exiles. A broad component relation cannot identify these groups as one organization.

621/2FF must retain Varennes accelerating new émigré arrivals and alarm. Correct the inherited 172 placement: full 171 supports Rhineland organization, 172 monarchic alarm, and 173 officer losses. Artois had settled before the flight, so not every centre began because of it.

Reject the normalized enables direction when the old source operator is enabled_by. E268 should preserve Wolfe Tone’s persuasion and United Irish preparations as encouragement, with the source’s doubts about a mass rising and the failed landing.

032D can internalize the 1793 constitution as an immediate demand within a wider insurrectionary programme. Preserve deeper equality/property aims and their narrower appeal rather than identifying constitutional restoration with the whole programme.

7593/DCF7/C479 and C389 must retain the manifesto within the 1792 intervention, émigré influence and counterproductive threats. An includes relation alone is weaker than the source’s political consequence and must not erase it.

B888/0364/7EDE/2E013 must preserve peace as a domestic fault line crossing a simple royalist/republican divide. Pragmatic Directors could favour conciliation; victorious generals and executive hardliners feared restoration and loss of conquests.

1D983 can internalize Provence’s regency claim followed by kingship after Louis XVII’s death, preserving disputed leadership, foreign dependence and changing strategy. Do not retroactively call every earlier action an act of a reigning Louis XVIII.

Reject a misleading active expresses direction if it reverses expressed-through; preserve the real organizational visibility of the 1799 revival in Manège within 3F2B. Distinguish this phase from earlier Pantheon and constitutional circles.

5B270 can internalize repression of refractory clergy within Second Directory anti-clerical policy. Retain the new oath, deportation liability and practical limits, rather than treating the retired broad label as proof of comprehensive enforcement.

5193/F6ED must retain depreciation crippling state payments and receipts, while mandates are a later failed response. Monetary and fiscal collapse interacted; avoid assigning the initial assignat mechanism solely to the successor currency.

6EF8/B438 must preserve military pressure combined with religious concessions in pacification. C4FA may support the foreign-aid context but is not itself evidence of religious détente or Hoche’s domestic policy.

7549 must retain the contrast between localized vengeance and purposeful national electioneering; B888 is a usable destination for the latter even though the original target was unbound. Retire the label, not the source’s distinction.

DE8A/9EDD can internalize deliberate right-wing encouragement of excess as an internal counter-revolutionary strategy. Distinguish it from ordinary conservative opposition and from externally organized invasion.

E268 can internalize United Irish advocacy and preparations enabling the expedition decision, with Tone and French domestic-strategic motives. Full 215–216 qualifies expected support and does not establish that a sufficient rising would actually occur.

B438/6EF8 must retain religious détente complementing coercive pacification. The two complementary directions describe one interaction, not proof that either element alone ended insurgency; keep foreign aid separate.

48B must retain Doyle’s judgment that an imminent restoration was improbable despite genuine agents and plots. Full 331 distinguishes absence of a royalist majority from denial of all danger and preserves plausible constitutional accommodation.

DE8A/7593 must retain the strategic difference between staying to obstruct and leaving to organize resistance. Later Quiberon and Condé are examples of external activity, not evidence that every émigré chose the same initial strategy.

Reject the reversed resentment-to-speculation cause. F6ED/4E189 must preserve mandates allowing cheap national-property purchases and enrichment provoking resentment; 59C’s general hardship mechanism does not alone preserve this precise connection.

6773 can internalize the pures/constitutionalists division within heterogeneous counter-revolution. Preserve cooperation and conflict at specific moments rather than presenting a permanent unified programme.

E268/2E013 must retain the Irish expedition plan helping precipitate rejection of the 1796 peace overtures. Full 215–216 supports the decision sequence; the failed voyage was not an interruption after a successful treaty.
C479/069F must retain foreign powers’ priorities, conditional support and rivalry as contributors to failure. Avoid both absence-of-all-aid and unconditional-restorationist interpretations.

AB9E/7593 can internalize Calonne and the Turin committee organizing early émigré action. Do not project the same leadership over all later Quiberon or Condé operations simply because old scope split into those parents.

21A/48B must retain military dependence making Fructidor possible and helping motivate intervention. The coup was a contingent coalition of Directors and generals; dependence alone is not a sufficient deterministic cause.

5193/F6ED must preserve post-paper deflation and scarce coin as part of the ensuing fiscal crisis, not merely as something following an independently defined later crisis. Retire the unresolved label and retain the actual monetary sequence.
5643/0D88 can internalize Barras’s command and Bonaparte’s artillery advice at Vendémiaire. Preserve substantial fighting and the source’s rejection of the later few-shells myth.
Reject ends: Babeuf and Buonarroti’s arrest did not end Directory repression of Jacobin organization. 032D must retain betrayal/arrest and later trial; 3F2B preserves subsequent repression phases.

33CF/04E7 must retain the princes’ use of Pillnitz as apparent foreign encouragement against the constitution. Keep the declaration’s conditional character distinct from the princes’ interpretation and later manifesto.

F6ED/4E189 must retain mandate depreciation enabling national-property speculation and resentment. This specific land-acquisition mechanism is not interchangeable with the generic paper-money hardship edge 59C.

7593 can internalize Koblenz militarization within émigré activity. Preserve specific foreign subsidies, forces and dates; later Quiberon/Condé parents should receive only their genuinely related phases.

5193/F6ED can internalize demonetization followed by deflation and specie scarcity. Page 333 supplies later continuing scarcity; retain 324 for the transition and avoid treating the end of paper as immediate financial recovery.
